description:
Tilde expansion, with and without a home directory, and in assignment-like words.

A Golem agent starts with no HOME and has no passwd entry. Bash then expands `~` to `/`, and so
does this shell; `cd` with no operand still fails with `HOME not set`.

Outside POSIX mode, bash also expands a tilde after the first `=` (and after each `:`) of any
command-line word that looks like an assignment, as in `make DESTDIR=~/out`.

cases.name: tilde: no home directory expands to /
cases.script: unset HOME; echo ~ ~/x "~"; d=~/y; echo $d; p=a:~:b; echo $p; cd ~; echo cd=$? $PWD; echo "${HOME-unset}"

cases.name: tilde: cd with no HOME fails and the script continues
cases.script: unset HOME; cd /tmp; cd 2>/dev/null; echo status=$? $PWD

cases.name: tilde: HOME set
cases.script: HOME=/tmp/h; mkdir -p ~/d; cd ~/d; pwd; echo ~ ~/x; cd; pwd; echo ~+ ~-

cases.name: tilde: quoted and mid-word tildes stay literal
tilde: assignment-like arguments
cases.script: HOME=/tmp/h; echo x=~/y x=~ x+=~ a[1]=~/z x=a:~/b:~ y=x=~

cases.name: tilde: arguments that are not assignment-like stay literal
cases.script: HOME=/tmp/h; echo --prefix=~/x 1x=~ x-y=~ "x=~" x="~" x=a~ x=a:"~" {x=~,y}

cases.name: tilde: assignment-like for, case and test words
cases.script: HOME=/tmp/h; for w in x=~ y=~/z; do echo "$w"; done; case x=/tmp/h in x=~) echo case-matched;; esac; [[ x=~ == x=/tmp/h ]] && echo double; [ x=~ = x=/tmp/h ] && echo single; f() { echo "$1"; }; f x=~; bash -c 'echo x=~/child'

cases.name: tilde: values, array elements, parameter words and here-strings
cases.script: HOME=/tmp/h; y=x=~:~; echo "$y"; a=(x=~ q); echo "${a[0]}"; echo "${u:-x=~}"; cat <<< x=~

cases.name: tilde: assignment-like redirect target
cases.script: HOME=/tmp/h; cd /tmp; mkdir -p x=/tmp/h; echo hi > x=~/f; cat x=/tmp/h/f

cases.name: tilde: POSIX mode keeps arguments literal
cases.script: HOME=/tmp/h; set -o posix; echo x=~/y; export Z=~/z; echo $Z
